feature: Behavior-preserving modularization of skills/ratchet-orchestrator/scripts/ratchet.py into coherent modules, keeping ratchet.py as the stable CLI entry point
next: CP1: spawn ratchet-implementer for this checkpoint only, then run: ratchet.py implemented CP1

objective.users: Rahil and the AI agents he directs, who read, review and extend Ratchet's own engine code in skills/ratchet-orchestrator/scripts/ratchet.py
objective.goal: Find and safely change any one responsibility of the engine (config, locks, provider discovery, run bookkeeping, plan/status reporting) without reading or risking the rest of a 21,000+ line file, while every existing command, test and tamper/lock guarantee keeps behaving exactly as before
done_means: ratchet.py --help, status --json, hook replies and failure exit codes are provably unchanged after every extraction in this run

Utility, fingerprint, tamper-evidence/locking, provider-discovery, run-bookkeeping/hook-env/integrity, and plan-validation/digest/plain-language-status code each move into their own module with explicit non-star imports, no circular imports and no new global mutable registry
Locking, tamper evidence, provider fallback and gate-support decisions keep their exact current behavior; nothing is weakened to make a move easier

Every source-inspection or module-loading test that reads ratchet.py's text or AST (43+ files found by grep, including the 5 named in the brief) is re-pointed to the new module locations in the same checkpoint that moves the code it inspects, keeping its actual invariant
The complete local suite (tests/run_all.py under the director's suite lock) passes after every checkpoint
A concise module map doc lists what moved and where, cross-referenced from README/SKILL.md
out_of_scope: Moving the hooks section (~2,465 lines: prompt/stop hook handlers, guard/command-safety checks, hook installation) — too large for one reviewable checkpoint; left for a dedicated follow-up feature
Moving the three giant single-function command handlers cmd_init (~825 lines), cmd_lanes_start + cmd_integrate (~1,527 lines), and cmd_ask (~571 lines) — each needs its own focused feature

Moving director approvals/signing (director-signed approvals, director_policy, director_sign, director_key/enroll, ~900 lines) — large and security-sensitive; deferred to its own feature so it gets full attention

Moving receipts, spec tools (OpenSpec/Spec Kit/BMAD import), shortcut tables, viewer/dashboard, CI export, reviewers/reviewer_status, guardrail/scoped-diff/occurrences/repeats, review-signing, and the _Watch/cmd_red/cmd_behavior gate-running machinery — all deferred to follow-up features
Extracting main()'s argparse setup and dispatch, and the top-level _StateLock/_IntegrateLock — these intentionally stay in ratchet.py as the stable, thin entry point, per done-means #1
Any behavior change not explicitly called out and approved as a scope decision
New user configuration, reviewer-policy changes, or OpenCode hook behavior changes
Refactoring the internals of any giant function being moved (e.g. splitting cmd_init's body into smaller functions) — this run moves code verbatim only
